Pipeline / Stage conversion

Lead-to-customer conversion

The percentage of unique valid leads in a defined intake cohort that become new paying customers within an agreed conversion window. It measures the complete journey after lead capture, rather than a platform's conversion-event count.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The percentage of unique valid leads in a defined intake cohort that become new paying customers within an agreed conversion window. It measures the complete journey after lead capture, rather than a platform's conversion-event count.

%

How we use it

Shows whether acquisition, nurturing, and sales work together. We can break this into intermediate stages to locate leakage and route follow-up actions.

Transparent calculationLeads in the cohort becoming paying customers within the window ÷ unique valid leads in that cohort × 100
cohort leads120
converted cohort leads12

12 ÷ 120 × 100 = 10%. All 12 customers came from the same 120-lead cohort.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Lead acquisition cohort
  • Source and customer segment
  • Offer and sales owner

Questions we investigate

  • Are numerator customers from the original lead cohort?
  • Which sources convert qualified interest into payment?
  • Are cohorts mature and deduplicated?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Track lead-to-customer membership consistently.
  • Investigate drop-off across intermediate stages.
  • Improve follow-up and the buying experience.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Revenue operations lead
Monthly for cohorts with the complete conversion window.

Required data

  • Unique valid starting lead cohort
  • Linked first-payment customer outcomes
  • Conversion deadline and eligibility policy

Read the measure with context

Zero cohort leads makes the rate undefined. Recently captured leads may not have completed the sales cycle. Specify person versus account identity and conversion window. Customers from earlier cohorts must not inflate the numerator.
